notes: Focused forward-test set for the v1.6.0 structural refactor. These prompts verify that progressive disclosure preserves a framework-specific lifecycle correction, the two proactive UX review reflexes, and the output contract for a bounded picker. Assertions define the grading rubric; comparative results require a recorded harness run with provider/model metadata.

evals.name: bubble-tea-cleanup-after-slimming
evals.prompt: Review this Bubble Tea shutdown pattern before I ship it: `p := tea.NewProgram(model); defer p.RestoreTerminal(); _, err := p.Run(); return err`. I added the defer to make sure a panic cannot leave the terminal broken. Is this correct, and what should I use instead?
assertions: Says the defer is incorrect and should be removed
Explains that RestoreTerminal resumes Bubble Tea terminal mode after ReleaseTerminal rather than performing final shell cleanup
Explains that Bubble Tea's normal Run lifecycle and default panic handling clean up the terminal
Does not recommend redundant custom cleanup on the managed path; any custom outer boundary is limited to bypassing or disabling framework-managed cleanup

evals.name: kubernetes-browser-clutter-and-floor
evals.prompt: Review my Kubernetes resource browser layout. At 140 columns it has a double-line outer frame around the whole terminal, then three bordered panes: namespaces, resources, and YAML. Every resource row begins with a bullet and ends with a green `[READY]` plus a checkmark. The bottom two rows list 18 keyboard shortcuts. There is no responsive behavior yet because most of us use wide monitors. What would you change before release?
assertions: Runs a concrete clutter audit: identifies the redundant outer frame or border nesting and recommends a specific cut
Counts the duplicate readiness signals and recognizes that a marker on every row marks nothing
Replaces the 18-key wall with a small contextual hint set plus discoverable full help
Raises responsive behavior unprompted and gives concrete behavior at 80x24, 60 columns, and an application-specific minimum
Requires a single-pane or drill-down fallback rather than merely shrinking three columns

evals.name: branch-picker-output-contract
evals.prompt: I need a small Go tool that lets someone pick one of their recent git branches with fuzzy search, then use it in `git checkout $(branchpick)`. I want the invoking command and chosen branch to remain visible in scrollback. Should this be a full-screen Bubble Tea app? Describe the output contract, terminal mode, and the most important implementation and test choices.
assertions: Recommends a bounded inline picker rather than a full-screen alternate-screen session because scrollback should remain visible
Places the selected branch alone on stdout and interactive UI or diagnostics on stderr or /dev/tty so command substitution remains safe
Uses current Bubble Tea v2 mechanics by leaving View.AltScreen false or unset, without recommending removed v1-only options as current API
Keeps git/subprocess work outside Update and returns results through a tea.Cmd or message
Tests state transitions and a pinned small rendered size, plus an integration check that stdout contains only the selected value and cancel/failure returns a meaningful nonzero status
